title: tapHLE clickmap
description: A replayable record of how to drive one app to a rating milestone. Written once by whoever reached the milestone, replayed by everyone after. See protocol.md.

clickmap_version.description: Format version. Bump only for incompatible changes; a runner that does not recognise the value must refuse to replay rather than guess.

app.description: Identity as printed by `tapHLE --info`. Never copied from a filename.

version.description: The version this map was recorded against. A different version is worth TRYING this map on -- that is the point of the format -- but a mismatch must be reported, never hidden.

sha256.description: Of the exact artifact, so a replay can say whether it tested the same bytes.

recorded.description: Provenance of the recording. A map that never replayed is a hypothesis.

taphle_version.description: Committed revision it was recorded on. Never a -dirty one.

host.description: Free text, e.g. "Windows 11, Intel Iris Xe". Timings are host-dependent.

options.description: Launch options the map assumes, as they appear in tapHLE_default_options.txt. Empty array means none. If this disagrees with the options file, the options file wins and the replay must report the difference.

window.description: Client-area size the coordinates below are in. A replay that gets a different size must NOT rescale silently: report and stop.

rating.description: 2 = reaches a stable screen; 3 = a gameplay loop that starts and persists. An agent may not assert 4 or 5.

describes.description: One sentence: what a human would see at the end.

defaults.description: Applied to any step that does not override them.

press_ms.description: Some apps ignore a press shorter than their own polling interval.

settle_ms.description: Wait after the action before the next step.

notes.description: Traps a replayer needs and cannot infer: input that is invisible on screen, a capture whose axes differ from client coordinates, a screen that animates after a missed tap and so looks like it responded.

id.description: Stable name, so a report can say which step failed without counting.

from.description: The screen this step starts on, in the words a human would use.

action.description: tap takes at/press_ms; swipe takes from_xy/to_xy/duration_ms; type takes text; key takes scancode; wait takes only settle_ms; capture takes only expect.

scancode.description: PS/2 set 1 scancode, e.g. 28 for Return. Recorded as a scancode because SDL does not see a virtual-key-only synthetic press.

expect.description: What should be on screen after this step, in plain words. The runner cannot check it; it goes in the report so an agent reading a failed replay knows what it was looking for. THIS is what saves the tokens: an agent screenshots only where a replay says it stopped.

optional.description: True for steps that depend on state the app may or may not have -- dismissing a first-run prompt, a rate nag, a tutorial already seen. A replay that finds the screen absent skips the step and says so, rather than failing.

requires_save_state.description: absent: only run on a fresh profile. present: only run when a save exists. This is the usual reason a map that worked yesterday diverges today -- see protocol.md.
